payload.name: Alice
payload.note: The young girl protagonist of Wonderland, the dreamer and main witness, present across all twelve divisions under varied aliases (the little girl, the child, the girl, Mary Ann by mistake); her sister is a separate person and is not in this group.

stages.label: Alice
stages.text: Alice: a young Victorian English girl of about seven or eight, slender and small-boned with a child's build, fair skin, long loose hair that falls into her bright eager eyes and is tossed back from her face, and a round, earnest face. She wears a Victorian child's dress with a pinafore over it, with stockings and buttoned shoes on her feet, and carries nothing else of note.

quotes.quote: Oh, my poor little feet, I wonder who will put on your shoes and stockings for you now, dears?
the bright eager eyes were looking up into hers
three inches is such a wretched height to be

payload.name: Alice's sister
payload.note: Alice's unnamed older sister, who sits on the bank with a book, wakes Alice, and dreams of Wonderland; both entries describe the same individual.

stages.label: Alice's sister
stages.text: Alice's sister: an older young Victorian English woman in her late teens or early twenties, slender build, fair skin, dark hair pinned up neatly. She wears a plain, modest Victorian day dress with a high neck and long sleeves in muted blue-grey, with a simple shawl. Her signature prop is a small book she holds closed in her lap or on the grass beside her.

quotes.quote: sitting by her sister on the bank
with her head in the lap of her sister, who was gently brushing away some dead leaves

payload.name: White Rabbit
aliases: the White Rabbit with pink eyes
payload.note: The one talking white rabbit with pink eyes and a waistcoat-pocket watch, who hurries Alice down the hole, owns the house, sends for gloves and a fan, and later serves as the court's herald and reader of the verses. All six entries are this same rabbit, so they stay together in this cluster.

stages.label: White Rabbit
stages.text: White Rabbit: an anthropomorphic white rabbit, upright and human-proportioned, with pink eyes, white fur, and a small, anxious build. Dressed in a splendid waistcoat with a pocket holding a pocket watch, often carrying white kid gloves and a large fan, and as herald at court a trumpet and a rolled parchment scroll. Fussy and hurried in manner, with a waistcoat and whiskers as his most distinctive features.

quotes.quote: a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her
took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket
splendidly dressed, with a pair of white kid gloves in one hand and a large fan in the other
with a trumpet in one hand, and a scroll of parchment in the other

payload.name: Dinah
payload.note: Alice's pet cat, mentioned only and never physically present in any division; all four entries (called the cat or our cat) describe the same animal at home, so they form one cluster.

payload.name: The riverbank
payload.note: The grassy bank beside which Alice sits with her sister, where the White Rabbit runs past and where her sister dreams at sunset; both entries describe this same bank, so they form one place.

stages.label: The riverbank
stages.text: The riverbank: a grassy bank sloping gently to a slow river, with a wide open field beyond and a thick hedge along its edge where a large rabbit-hole opens among the roots. Tall trees stand nearby, their branches shedding dry leaves onto the grass. Wildflowers, including daisies, grow through the turf. The light of an English summer afternoon falls warm and soft over the field.

quotes.quote: sitting by her sister on the bank
ran across the field after it
pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge
found herself lying on the bank
dead leaves that had fluttered down from the trees

payload.name: The rabbit-hole
aliases: the large rabbit-hole under the hedge
payload.note: A deep tunnel under the hedge that dips into a long, deep well lined with cupboards and shelves. Units 3-10.

stages.label: The rabbit-hole
stages.text: The rabbit-hole: a tunnel under a hedge that runs straight for a way, then dips suddenly into a very deep well of dark earth. The well's walls are lined with cupboards, book-shelves, maps and pictures hung on wooden pegs. Near the bottom lies a heap of dry sticks and leaves on the earth floor, with a few hedge roots at the tunnel's mouth.

quotes.quote: The rabbit-hole went straight on like a tunnel for some way, and then dipped suddenly down
then she looked at the sides of the well, and noticed that they were filled with cupboards and book-shelves; here and there she saw maps and pictures hung upon pegs
down she came upon a heap of sticks and dry leaves

payload.name: The long low hall
payload.note: The single long, low hall with a glass table and a small door behind a curtain, where Alice grows and shrinks; the three entries are different visits to the same hall, not separate places.

stages.label: The long low hall
stages.text: The Long Low Hall: a long, low hall of smooth stone floor and low timber-beamed ceiling, stretching far in length and little in height, its roof hung with a row of lamps that light it evenly. Doors line all its walls, every one locked. Near the middle stands a small three-legged table of solid glass, and beside one wall a low curtain hides a little door about fifteen inches high. Vegetation is absent; the hall is an enclosed interior that opens only to a garden beyond the small door and a tree-door at the far end.

quotes.quote: a long, low hall, which was lit up by a row of lamps hanging from the roof
There were doors all round the hall, but they were all locked
a little three-legged table, all made of solid glass
a low curtain she had not noticed before, and behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high
until there was a large pool all round her, about four inches deep and reaching half down the hall

payload.name: The little door to the garden
aliases: The little door and passage to the garden
payload.note: The small fifteen-inch door in the hall that leads to a passage and the garden, locked with a little golden key on a glass table; both entries describe this same door, so they belong together.

stages.label: The little door to the garden
stages.text: The little door to the garden: a low door about fifteen inches high, set behind a hanging curtain in a long hall, its wood dark and old with a small golden keyhole. Beyond it a narrow passage no larger than a rat-hole leads into a sunlit garden of bright flower beds and cool fountains, glimpsed only faintly. Nearby stands a small three-legged table of solid glass, with a tiny golden key lying on its top.

quotes.quote: behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high
a little three-legged table, all made of solid glass
it led into a small passage, not much larger than a rat-hole
the loveliest garden you ever saw

payload.name: The Mouse
payload.note: The one mouse of the Pool of Tears who swims with Alice, is offended by talk of cats and dogs, lectures on English history, tells the long tale about Fury, and storms off; the same individual in both divisions, so no other mouse in this group needs separating.

stages.label: The Mouse
stages.text: The Mouse: a small grey-brown mouse with round ears, bright little eyes and a long thin tail, standing upright with human posture; it wears a modest Victorian waistcoat and a small hat, and its fur bristles and it trembles when offended. Small and wet from swimming, with fur clinging close.

quotes.quote: it was only a mouse that had slipped in like herself
The Mouse looked at her rather inquisitively, and seemed to her to wink with one of its little eyes
who was trembling down to the end of his tail
looking down with wonder at the Mouse’s tail

payload.name: Ada
payload.note: A girl of Alice's age whom Alice considers as a possible identity in unit 10; not present.

payload.name: Mabel
payload.note: A girl of Alice's age whom Alice considers as a possible identity in units 10 and 13; not present.

payload.name: the Duck
payload.note: The one duck in the wet gathering of birds and animals, first in the Pool of Tears swim to shore and again in the Caucus-Race, where it questions the Mouse. Both entries describe the same duck.

stages.label: the Duck
stages.text: the Duck: a waterfowl the size of a large domestic duck, standing upright on two webbed feet with human posture, wearing a Victorian waistcoat and small hat. Plumage is a glossy white-grey with orange-yellow bill and feet, feathers draggled and wet from the pool. Its manner is brisk and argumentative, a dry, practical bird among the dripping company.

quotes.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet
the birds with draggled feathers, the animals with their fur clinging close to them, and all dripping wet
“Found _what_?” said the Duck.

payload.name: the Dodo
payload.note: The Dodo, a bird who is among those fallen into the pool, swims ashore with the party, and later proposes the Caucus-race, runs it, awards the prizes and presents Alice's thimble; both entries describe the same bird.

stages.label: the Dodo
stages.text: the Dodo: an elderly, portly dodo bird standing upright on two legs with human posture, with a plump grey-brown body, a large hooked bill, small wings held at its sides, and a rounded head. It wears a Victorian waistcoat and cravat with a dignified, pompous bearing, and carries no props of its own. Its plumage is dry in the scene described.

quotes.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet
said the Dodo solemnly, rising to its feet
the Dodo solemnly presented the thimble

payload.name: the Lory
payload.note: The Lory, a bird from the caucus gathering who swims ashore from the pool and later argues with Alice about age and laments the Mouse leaving; both divisions describe the same bird.

stages.label: The Lory
stages.text: The Lory: an adult parrot-like bird of middling age with draggled, dripping feathers in bright green, a short hooked beak and a sulky, self-important bearing. Its plumage is glossy green with red and yellow patches on wings and breast, fur-free and damp from the pool. Its signature accessory is none; it carries no props. Dress: none beyond its own feathers.

quotes.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet
the Lory, who at last turned sulky, and would only say, "I am older than you, and must know better;"
"What a pity it wouldn't stay!" sighed the Lory

payload.name: the Eaglet
payload.note: A young eaglet among the birds that fell into the Pool of Tears and gathered on the bank for the Caucus-Race; both entries describe this same bird, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: Eaglet
stages.text: The Eaglet: a young eaglet, a juvenile bird of prey not yet full-grown, with downy-feathered body, brown-tawny plumage, and a sharp hooked beak and yellow-tipped talons. Its feathers are draggled and wet from the Pool of Tears, clinging close to its body. Its signature colours are warm brown and tawny with pale patches of down. It carries no props.

quotes.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet
"Speak English!" said the Eaglet.

payload.name: Pool creatures
aliases: the birds and animals that had fallen into it
payload.note: The crowd of birds and animals that fell into the pool and swim together to the shore in unit 26.

stages.label: Pool creatures
stages.text: Pool creatures: a mixed crowd of waterlogged birds and animals, typical member a small feathered or furred creature of modest size, drenched plumage or fur clinging to the body, upright human-like posture with dampened Victorian-era waistcoats or small garments where dress is given, a Duck, a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet among varied curious species, muted earthy and grey tones with wet sheen, whimsical dreamlike Victorian Wonderland styling.

quotes.quote: the birds and animals that had fallen into it: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet
several other curious creatures

payload.name: the Duchess
payload.note: The short-tempered Duchess of the kitchen, who nurses the baby and sings the lullaby, later walks with Alice, is sent away by the Queen, and is named again as the imprisoned Duchess under sentence of execution; the Pool of Tears mention is the Rabbit hurrying to her. Only one Duchess appears in this work's divisions.

stages.label: The Duchess
stages.text: The Duchess: a woman of middle years with a very ugly, sharp-chinned face and a pointed, narrow chin, of a height to rest her chin on a young girl's shoulder. Build slight and bony. Skin pale and sallow. Dark hair pinned up under a large, lopsided Victorian cap. Signature outfit worn most often: a dark brown or plum Victorian gown with a high collar and a shawl of faded green, colours muted. Carries a baby wrapped in a shawl when in the kitchen; no other props.

quotes.quote: the Duchess was sitting on a three-legged stool in the middle, nursing a baby
because the Duchess was _very_ ugly; and secondly, because she was exactly the right height to rest her chin upon Alice’s shoulder, and it was an uncomfortably sharp chin

payload.name: Pool of Tears
aliases: the pool of tears which she had wept
payload.note: The body of water formed from Alice's tears, where Alice swims with the Mouse and the birds and animals swim; distinct from the shore, which is the bank.

stages.label: Pool of Tears
stages.text: Pool of Tears: a broad body of salt water filling the long hall, formed from Alice's own tears, shallow at its edges and deep enough to swim in at its middle, its surface pale and still under a low, dim dream-light. Its banks are smooth, rounded edges of the hall floor, and it is surrounded by the hall's tall walls, a little golden key and a small garden door in the distance.

quotes.quote: shedding gallons of tears, until there was a large pool all round her, about four inches deep
up to her chin in salt water

payload.name: Shore
payload.note: The shore of the pool to which Alice leads the swimming party in unit 26.

stages.label: Shore
stages.text: Shore: the grassy edge of the pool of tears, a gentle sloping bank of pale pebbles and short green turf, with tufts of reeds and a few low bushes along the water's rim. The pool's broad, salt-tinged water lies beside it, and the bank rises to a soft meadow of wild grass and clover under an open Wonderland sky, with a dry stone outcrop jutting out toward the water.

quotes.quote: the whole party swam to the shore.
Let us get to the shore, and then I'll tell you my history

payload.name: the old Magpie
payload.note: An old magpie who wraps itself up and leaves after Alice mentions cats.

stages.label: the old Magpie
stages.text: the old Magpie: an elderly magpie drawn as an animal with a plump, rounded body, glossy black and white plumage, a long dark tail, a short stout beak and bright, shrewd eyes. Human posture and a shawl or wrap of muted Victorian tweed drawn tightly about its body, in keeping with the animal's dress in the text. Its signature prop is the wrap it draws around itself.

quotes.quote: one old Magpie began wrapping itself up very carefully
the night-air doesn't suit my throat

payload.name: the Canary
payload.note: A canary who calls its children away to bed after Alice mentions cats.

stages.label: the Canary
stages.text: the Canary: an adult songbird of middling age, small and plump-breasted, with bright yellow plumage and a rounded head, standing upright on two slender legs in human posture. It wears a neat Victorian bonnet and a little shawl over a soft dress of pale yellow, with a demure white collar. It carries no props.

quotes.quote: a Canary called out in a trembling voice to its children
Come away, my dears! It's high time you were all in bed!

payload.name: the old Crab (mother of the young Crab)
payload.note: The old Crab in the Caucus race who scolds her daughter about losing her temper; told apart from the Classics master by being the mother of the young Crab in the Caucus-race section.

stages.label: the old Crab
stages.text: the old Crab: an elderly female crab of the Wonderland company, drawn as a crab with human posture and dress. Age: elderly. Build: stout, rounded shell. Shell: mottled reddish-brown carapace, pale underside, claws held in front. Eyes: small stalked eyes on the shell's front edge. Signature outfit: a dark bonnet and a faded brown shawl over a grey dress, the colours of a respectable matron. Signature props: none.

quotes.quote: an old Crab took the opportunity of saying to her daughter

payload.name: the young Crab
payload.note: A young crab, daughter of the old Crab, who snaps back at her mother.

stages.label: The young Crab
stages.text: The young Crab: a young crab, a daughter of the old crab, smaller and more youthful than her mother, with a bright red-orange shell, ten jointed legs, and two stalked eyes on the front of the head, drawn as an animal with a slightly upright, impatient posture and a small pair of clasping claws. She has a sharp, peevish manner and a touch of pert youthful defiance.

quotes.quote: Hold your tongue, Ma!” said the young Crab, a little snappishly.
You’re enough to try the patience of an oyster!

payload.name: the assembled birds and animals
payload.note: The wet gathering on the bank who sit in a ring, race, and chorus their requests as one body.

stages.label: the assembled birds and animals
stages.text: the assembled birds and animals: a mixed group of birds with draggled, dripping feathers and small animals with fur clinging close to their bodies, all soaked through, in the manner of talking animals in human dress; typical member an adult creature standing upright with human posture, wearing a waterlogged waistcoat or shawl in faded Victorian colours, damp and bedraggled throughout.

quotes.quote: the birds with draggled feathers, the animals with their fur clinging close to them, and all dripping wet

payload.name: The bank of the pool of tears
aliases: the bank of the pool of tears
payload.note: The shore of the pool of tears where the wet party assembles, dries off, holds the Caucus-Race and the Mouse's tale, and where Alice is left alone; distinct from the opening riverbank.

stages.label: The bank of the pool of tears
stages.text: The bank of the pool of tears: a grassy shore of a salt-water pool, its edge damp and soft underfoot, with low tufts of wet grass and a few stunted reeds at the waterline. A broad, level clearing of trodden turf rises gently from the water, set with a few scattered mushrooms and a low bush or two, and a wide circular track worn into the grass for the Caucus-race. Pale, drifting mist hangs over the still pool, which spreads out of frame toward the far side, and a faint salty glimmer lies on the water.

quotes.quote: They were indeed a queer-looking party that assembled on the bank
First it marked out a race-course, in a sort of circle

payload.name: Mary Ann
payload.note: The Rabbit's housemaid, only named and never seen on stage; a separate person from Alice, whom the Rabbit confuses with her.

payload.name: Pat
payload.note: The Rabbit's gardener, an Irishman (speaks with an Irish dialect) who is outside the window and handles the arm; he is heard but not seen.

stages.label: Pat
stages.text: Pat: a middle-aged Irish gardener, sturdy and weathered, with a broad build and ruddy, sun-browned skin. Short, tousled hair under a battered cap, with stubble on his jaw and a rough, good-natured face. He wears a rough linen shirt with rolled sleeves, a patched waistcoat, and dark corduroy trousers tucked into worn boots, in muted earth tones. He carries a spade or garden tool.

quotes.quote: Sure then I’m here! Digging for apples, yer honour!
Sure, it’s an arm, yer honour!

payload.name: Bill the Lizard
payload.note: Bill the Lizard, the lizard sent down the chimney by the Rabbit's servants and kicked out by Alice, who later serves as a juror at the trial and writes on a slate; the three entries are one individual across divisions.

stages.label: Bill the Lizard
stages.text: Bill the Lizard: a small, feeble lizard of modest size, slender body, scaled skin in muted green, long tail, and small clawed feet, dressed in a little juror's waistcoat and cravat in the Victorian manner of the court. Bill stands upright on hind legs with human posture, holds a small slate and a pencil, and has a tuft of ink-stained scales on the face. Drawn as an animal with human dress where the text gives it, and small enough to be sent down a chimney.

quotes.quote: Bill’s to go down—Here, Bill!
Last came a little feeble, squeaking voice
The poor little Lizard, Bill, was in the middle, being held up by two guinea-pigs
the poor little juror (it was Bill, the Lizard)
all except the Lizard, who seemed too much overcome to do anything but sit with its mouth open

payload.name: the two guinea-pigs
payload.note: A pair of guinea-pigs who serve the Rabbit, first holding up Bill outside the house and rushing at Alice, then cheering in court until the officers bag them; no note separates them from each other, so they are kept as one pair.

stages.label: Rabbit's guinea-pig servants
stages.text: The two guinea-pigs: a pair of plump, short-legged guinea-pigs standing upright in human posture, each in a small Victorian servant's waistcoat and neat cap, with glossy brown and cream coats and round dark eyes. They serve the Rabbit as attentive footmen, attending to small bottles and cheering in court.

quotes.quote: being held up by two guinea-pigs, who were giving it something out of a bottle
they slipped the guinea-pig, head first, and then sat upon it

payload.name: the puppy
payload.note: A large puppy in the wood that Alice plays with using a stick.

stages.label: the puppy
stages.text: the puppy: an enormous young dog, far larger than Alice, with a shaggy coat, large round eyes, floppy ears, big paws, and a bright pink tongue hanging from its open mouth. It has the stocky, gangly build of an oversized puppy, with a sturdy body and long legs that look too big for it. Its fur is soft and tawny-brown with lighter patches on the chest and muzzle. It wears no clothing and carries no props; a small stick may lie nearby but belongs to Alice.

quotes.quote: An enormous puppy was looking down at her with large round eyes
its tongue hanging out of its mouth, and its great eyes half shut

payload.name: the Caterpillar
payload.note: The large blue, languid Caterpillar smoking a hookah on a mushroom, who advises Alice in the Caterpillar sections; both entries describe this same individual, the only Caterpillar in the group.

stages.label: the Caterpillar
stages.text: the Caterpillar: a large blue caterpillar with a segmented, many-legged body and a human-like upper posture, arms folded across its chest, a languid sleepy face with heavy-lidded eyes, and a long hookah pipe in its mouth. It is an animal with human posture and dress where given, sitting atop a large round mushroom. Its signature props are the long hookah and the mushroom it sits on, both carried or perched upon alone. Blue body throughout.

quotes.quote: a large blue caterpillar, that was sitting on the top with its arms folded, quietly smoking a long hookah
rearing itself upright as it spoke (it was exactly three inches high)

payload.name: the White Rabbit's house
payload.note: A neat little house with a brass plate on the door; Alice grows inside its tidy room, with the stairs and window.)

stages.label: The White Rabbit's House
stages.text: The White Rabbit's House: a neat small Victorian cottage of warm red brick with a steep slate roof, a narrow chimney and a single small casement window set low in the wall. A bright brass plate engraved W. RABBIT is fixed to the front door, which opens inwards. Inside, a tidy little room has a small table set in the window, a looking-glass on the wall, and a narrow staircase rising to the upper rooms. Rooms are modest in scale, so the house visibly strains around a grown Alice.

quotes.quote: a neat little house, on the door of which was a bright brass plate with the name “W. RABBIT,” engraved upon it
a tidy little room with a table in the window
the door opened inwards

payload.name: the Rabbit's garden
payload.note: The area outside the Rabbit's house where Pat, Bill and the crowd of animals gather around the window and chimney.

stages.label: the Rabbit's garden
stages.text: the Rabbit's garden: a small cottage garden outside a low house with a small window and an inward-opening door, a sooty brick chimney and a slate roof with a loose slate, beside a cucumber-frame of glass panes, with a thick wood beyond the hedge and a patch of grass and hedge.

quotes.quote: tried to open it; but, as the door opened inwards
a crash of broken glass, from which she concluded that it was just possible it had fallen into a cucumber-frame
Will the roof bear?—Mind that loose slate
found quite a crowd of little animals and birds waiting outside

payload.name: The thick wood (Alice's first wood)
payload.note: The wood where Alice wanders after escaping the crowd, meets the puppy and finds the mushroom; distinct from the mushroom clearing within it and from the Duchess's woods.

stages.label: The thick wood
stages.text: The thick wood: a dense wood of tall trees and close-set trunks, with great thistles, tall grass, blades and flowers, buttercups at the edges, and a large mushroom about Alice's own height growing on the ground, in a dim dreamlike Victorian English woodland under soft indistinct light, with no people.

quotes.quote: as she wandered about in the wood
while she was peering about anxiously among the trees
Alice dodged behind a great thistle
as she leant against a buttercup to rest herself
There was a large mushroom growing near her, about the same height as herself

payload.name: the Pigeon
payload.note: An anxious mother Pigeon in a tree nest who mistakes Alice's long neck for a serpent's and accuses her of hunting eggs.

stages.label: The Pigeon
stages.text: The Pigeon: a large pigeon, an adult mother bird of middle age with a plump, rounded body and a broad chest, grey-blue feathers with darker wing bars, and a pale throat. Her head is small and round with a short, pointed beak, and bright, anxious eyes. She has human posture and dress, standing upright on two legs with arms and hands, wearing a simple dark shawl over her shoulders. Her signature prop is a single large twig-nest in the high branch of a tree.

quotes.quote: “Serpent!” screamed the Pigeon.
I must be on the look-out for serpents night and day!
I’ve seen a good many little girls in my time

payload.name: Father William
payload.note: The old man in Alice's recited poem who stands on his head and balances an eel; he speaks with his son, the young man, in the verses.

payload.name: the young man
payload.note: The son of Father William in Alice's recited poem, who questions his father; exists only within the poem's verses.

payload.name: The mushroom clearing
aliases: the open place in the wood
payload.note: The open clearing where the Caterpillar sits on a large round mushroom and where Alice nibbles it; a specific spot, not the wood at large.

stages.label: The mushroom clearing
stages.text: The mushroom clearing: an open place in a wood, with tall trees rising around its edge and grass underfoot. At its centre stands a large, perfectly round mushroom, broad enough to sit upon, with its flat cap rising above the grass. Dense tree-tops and a sea of green leaves lie beyond the clearing, and a small house stands at its far edge.

quotes.quote: as it was perfectly round, she found this a very difficult question
a little shaking among the distant green leaves
the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering
she came suddenly upon an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high

payload.name: the treetops
payload.note: The high tree where the Pigeon has its nest, among the trees under which Alice had been wandering.

stages.label: the treetops
stages.text: the treetops: the leafy crowns of tall trees in a wooded place, dense green foliage with interlacing branches, the highest tree rising above the rest, a broad wood of untrimmed oaks and elms, no people, no buildings, Victorian English dream landscape in the manner of Tenniel's engravings.

quotes.quote: the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering
just as I'd taken the highest tree in the wood

payload.name: the open place with the little house
aliases: the little house in the open place
payload.note: An open place with a small house about four feet high, which Alice approaches once she has shrunk to nine inches.

stages.label: Open place with the little house
stages.text: the open place with the little house: a clearing opening suddenly among the trees of a mushroom wood, with a small cottage about four feet high standing in it. The cottage is of plain Victorian country build, with a pitched roof, a low door and small windows, roughly the height of a child's doorway. Grass and low wild growth fill the clearing, and trees ring its edges.

quotes.quote: she came suddenly upon an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high

payload.name: Fish-Footman
payload.note: A footman, so called by Alice from his face, who delivers the Queen's invitation to the Duchess at the door and then sits staring at the sky; not the Frog-Footman.

stages.label: Fish-Footman
stages.text: Fish-Footman: adult man, slim to medium build, pale skin, face with a fish-like cast with wide mouth and large round eyes, powdered white hair curling all over his head, worn in the manner of a footman's wig. Signature outfit: a formal footman's livery coat with brass buttons, knee breeches and white stockings, in dark green and gold. Signature prop: a great letter, nearly as large as himself, carried under one arm.

quotes.quote: a footman in livery came running out of the wood
judging by his face only, she would have called him a fish
both footmen, Alice noticed, had powdered hair that curled all over their heads

payload.name: Frog-Footman
aliases: the footman with a round face and frog-like eyes
payload.note: The footman with a round face and large eyes who opens the door and repeats the invitation message; sits on the ground outside afterward.

stages.label: Frog-Footman
stages.text: Frog-Footman: adult manservant, slim and upright in build, pale skin, powdered white hair curled tightly all over the head, round face with large bulging frog-like eyes. Signature outfit: a formal footman's livery coat in deep green with brass buttons, white powdered wig-like curls, white stockings and dark knee breeches, worn with a buttoned waistcoat. No props carried alone.

quotes.quote: with a round face, and large eyes like a frog
both footmen, Alice noticed, had powdered hair that curled all over their heads
another footman in livery

payload.name: The Duchess's cook
payload.note: The Duchess's kitchen cook with a pepper-box, who stirs peppery soup in the kitchen scene and is later questioned about the tarts before vanishing; both entries are the same cook, linked by the kitchen, the Duchess and the pepper-box.

stages.label: The Duchess's cook
stages.text: The Duchess's cook: a stout woman in her middle years with a broad, sturdy build and rosy, flushed skin from the heat of the fire. Her hair is tucked under a plain white cap, and she wears a long dark Victorian kitchen dress with a white apron and sleeves rolled to the elbow. Her signature prop is a pepper-box she carries in her hand, and her face is set in a sour, determined expression.

quotes.quote: the cook was leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron which seemed to be full of soup
She carried the pepper-box in her hand

payload.name: Baby
payload.note: The Duchess's infant, sneezing and howling, which Alice carries outside and which turns into a pig, then runs off into the wood.

stages.label: Baby
stages.text: Baby: a young infant of indeterminate age, small and queer-shaped, with limbs that stick out in all directions, a very turn-up snout-like nose and unusually small eyes, its skin pale and flushed from sneezing. Wrapped in a plain Victorian infant's gown of pale cotton or flannel, with a soft knitted cap. Tousled fine hair, barely visible under the cap. Its pig-like features grow more pronounced as it transforms.

quotes.quote: it was a queer-shaped little creature, and held out its arms and legs in all directions
There could be no doubt that it had a _very_ turn-up nose, much more like a snout than a real nose
its eyes were getting extremely small for a baby
it was neither more nor less than a pig

payload.name: Cheshire Cat
payload.note: The grinning cat who talks with Alice, appearing in the Duchess's kitchen and in the trees or in the air over the croquet ground and vanishing; not Dinah, who is only mentioned.

stages.label: Cheshire Cat
stages.text: Cheshire Cat: a large grey-and-white striped tabby cat, adult, with a broad, wide, ear-to-ear grin, long claws and many teeth, drawn as an animal with no clothing or props. Its fur is short and tabby-striped, eyes wide and bright, ears pointed, with a long tail. Neither dressed nor armed; a plain, natural cat form.

quotes.quote: it had _very_ long claws and a great many teeth
vanished quite slowly, beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin

payload.name: March Hare
payload.note: The one anthropomorphic mad hare of the work, first glimpsed at his large house, then a tea-party host, then a witness at the trial; all three entries are one recurring character, distinguished only by scene.

stages.label: March Hare
stages.text: March Hare: an anthropomorphic brown hare with long upright ears and a wild, staring, mad expression, standing on two legs with human posture. Age: middle-aged adult. Build: lean and wiry. Skin: brown fur. Hair and beard: none beyond fur on the face and whiskers. Facial notes: large round eyes, twitching nose. Signature outfit: a rumpled waistcoat and frock coat in faded brown and buff, with a loosened cravat. Signature props: a teacup and saucer.

quotes.quote: the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur
the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it

payload.name: The Hatter
payload.note: The Mad Hatter, host of the tea-party and later first witness at the Queen's trial; the Cat's mention of a hatter living the other way is the same man, so all three entries join one cluster.

stages.label: The Hatter
stages.text: The Hatter: an adult man of middle years, lean and slightly stooped, with a pale, anxious face and untidy, uncut hair. He wears a tall battered top hat and a rumpled Victorian frock coat and waistcoat in faded browns and mustard, with a loose cravat. Signature props he carries alone: a chipped teacup, a slice of bread-and-butter, and a pocket watch he holds to his ear.

quotes.quote: Your hair wants cutting
He came in with a teacup in one hand and a piece of bread-and-butter in the other.
he had taken his watch out of his pocket, and was looking at it uneasily, shaking it every now and then, and holding it to his ear.
Take off your hat,” the King said to the Hatter.

payload.name: Queen of Hearts
payload.note: The short-tempered Queen of Hearts who orders executions, runs the croquet game and sits beside the King at the trial; all six entries (including the 'Queen' who sends the croquet invitation and the 'Queen' the Hatter recalls) are the same individual, so keep them together.

stages.label: Queen of Hearts
stages.text: Queen of Hearts: an adult woman of middle years, stately and severe, with a flat oblong playing-card body, arms and legs at the corners, and a heart-ornamented robe in crimson and scarlet. Pale skin, dark hair dressed high under a small crown of gold, sharp features and a stern expression. Signature outfit: a long crimson velvet gown with heart shapes and a gold-trimmed collar. Signature prop: a small golden sceptre.

quotes.quote: The Queen turned crimson with fury
The King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne

payload.name: Duchess's House
payload.note: A house standing in a wood, with a door opening into a smoky kitchen where the Duchess and cook are.Alice enters the kitchen here.

stages.label: Duchess's House
stages.text: Duchess's House: a modest house standing at the edge of a wood, with a plain front door and rough, weathered timber walls. Inside the door lies a large kitchen filled with thick smoke, a great fire burning at one end, a hearth with a large cauldron of soup hanging over the flames, a three-legged stool at the centre, and pots, pans, plates and dishes scattered about. Trees of the wood crowd close around the house.

quotes.quote: a footman in livery came running out of the wood
a most extraordinary noise going on within
The door led right into a large kitchen, which was full of smoke from one end to the other
the Duchess was sitting on a three-legged stool in the middle

payload.name: The woods around the Duchess's house
payload.note: The woods by the Duchess's house where the footmen run out, the pig escapes and the Cheshire Cat sits in a tree; tied to the Duchess's residence.

stages.label: The woods around the Duchess's house
stages.text: The woods around the Duchess's house: a dim, close wood of tall, shadowy trees with broad trunks and low spreading boughs, rooted in soft grass and tangled undergrowth beside a modest house with a stout front door. Dappled light falls through the leaves, and a faint path leads between the trunks toward the wider country. Several trees stand near the house, and the wood thickens into a dreamlike, slightly unsettling maze. No people are present.

quotes.quote: a footman in livery came running out of the wood
broke to pieces against one of the trees behind him
trot away quietly into the wood

payload.name: March Hare's House
payload.note: A large house with ear-shaped chimneys and a fur-thatched roof, where the March Hare is said to live; Alice approaches it at the end.

stages.label: March Hare's House
stages.text: March Hare's House: a very large house with tall chimneys shaped like ears and a steeply pitched roof thatched with fur, set in a shaded woodland clearing among old trees and mushrooms, with a quiet garden path leading up to its front. The house is rambling and wide, with several windows and a timbered Victorian-storybook look in the whimsical tradition of the work's illustrations.

quotes.quote: the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur
It was so large a house

payload.name: the Dormouse
payload.note: The sleeping Dormouse of the Mad Tea-Party, who tells the treacle-well story and is seated between the Hare and the Hatter, and also the same Dormouse who sits beside Alice and is ordered out of court in the trial; both entries are one character, distinguished only by scene.

stages.label: the Dormouse
stages.text: the Dormouse: a small, drowsy dormouse with a plump round body, soft grey-brown fur, round ears, a long thin tail and small dark eyes half-closed with sleep. Standing upright in human posture, it wears a modest Victorian waistcoat and neckcloth in muted dusty blue with a small pocket watch chain, and carries no props of its own. Its whiskers are long and pale.

quotes.quote: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep
in a hoarse, feeble voice
got up very sulkily and crossed over to the other side of the court

payload.name: Time
payload.note: Personified Time, with whom the Hatter has quarrelled; mentioned only and never present on stage.

payload.name: Elsie
payload.note: One of the three little sisters in the Dormouse's story, who lived at the bottom of a treacle-well; told of, not present.

payload.name: Lacie
payload.note: One of the three little sisters in the Dormouse's story, living in the treacle-well; told of, not present.

payload.name: Tillie
payload.note: One of the three little sisters in the Dormouse's story, living in the treacle-well; told of, not present.

payload.name: Tea-table under a tree
aliases: the table in front of the house
payload.note: A large table set out under a tree in front of a house, where the tea-party takes place.

stages.label: Tea-table under a tree
stages.text: Tea-table under a tree: a large table set out under a tree in front of a house, its long surface crowded with tea-things, teapots, cups, saucers, a milk-jug, bread-and-butter and a cluster of mismatched chairs at one end, with a large armchair; the tree's branches cast shade over it, and the house stands behind it in a Victorian English garden setting.

quotes.quote: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house
The table was a large one, but the three were all crowded together at one corner of it
she sat down in a large arm-chair at one end of the table
so many tea-things are put out here

payload.name: The wood after the tea-party
payload.note: The wood Alice picks her way through after leaving the March Hare's tea-party and before the tree-door to the garden; tied to the tea-party, not the Duchess's house.

stages.label: The wood after the tea-party
stages.text: The wood after the tea-party: a tangled, shaded woodland of close-growing trees with twisted trunks and undergrowth, lit by dappled daylight through the leaves. Among the trunks stands at least one tree with a small door set into its bark, leading inward. Ground is uneven with roots and fallen leaves, and the path winds between the trees. No people or animals are present.

quotes.quote: she picked her way through the wood
one of the trees had a door leading right into it

payload.name: The garden
aliases: the garden entrance by the rose-tree
payload.note: The beautiful garden of flower-beds and fountains reached through the tree-door, including its entrance by the rose-tree where the card gardeners paint the roses; the entrance is part of this same garden, not a separate place.

stages.label: The garden
stages.text: The garden: a beautiful walled garden of bright flower-beds and cool fountains, entered through a door set into a great tree. Near the entrance stands a large rose-tree with white roses, its blooms in need of paint. Neat flower-beds, clipped hedges, stone paths and splashing fountains fill the grounds beneath a Victorian dream-sky.

quotes.quote: found herself at last in the beautiful garden, among the bright flower-beds and the cool fountains
A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden: the roses growing on it were white

payload.name: Two
payload.note: One of the three card gardeners painting roses red; the one who explains the mistake to Alice. Tell him apart by his role as the spokesman; he is a playing card, not a human.

stages.label: Two, card gardener
stages.text: Two: a flat, oblong playing card gardener, not a human, with a head, arms and legs placed at the corners of the card. Painted in the pattern of the card pack with a spade-marked back, he is a card of the gardeners' suit, dressed as a humble gardener in a plain waistcoat with a brush in hand. His face is small and earnest, with a meek, worried expression, and he carries a paintbrush and a pot of red paint as his only props.

quotes.quote: there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red
these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners
Two began in a low voice, "Why the fact is, you see, Miss

payload.name: Five
payload.note: One of the three card gardeners; blames Seven for splashing paint and warns the others of the Queen's approach. Tell him apart by his blaming of Seven and his warning; he is a playing card.

stages.label: Five
stages.text: Five: a flat, oblong playing card gardener with a head, arms and legs placed at the corners, his back patterned like the rest of the pack. He holds a paint brush and wears the plain gardener's garb of the card pack, with paint splashed across his card face and clothing.

quotes.quote: there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red
Look out now, Five! Don't go splashing paint over me like that!

payload.name: Seven
payload.note: One of the three card gardeners; blamed by Five and the one who checks himself on seeing Alice. Tell him apart by being the one blamed by Five; he is a playing card.

stages.label: Seven, card gardener
stages.text: Seven: a flat, oblong playing card gardener with a head, arms and legs at the corners of the card body. Its face is simple and a little sulky, and its card back carries the same pattern as the rest of the pack. Seven holds a paintbrush and is stained with red paint from the white roses it has been painting.

quotes.quote: there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red
these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners
the pattern on their backs was the same as the rest of the pack

payload.name: King of Hearts
payload.note: The mild, timid husband of the Queen who pardons the condemned, tries to protect Alice, and sits as judge at the trial; told apart from the Queen by his gentle, merciful conduct.

stages.label: King of Hearts
stages.text: King of Hearts: a mild, timid middle-aged man with a rounded, gentle face and a kindly, worried expression, a short full beard and moustache, and a plump build. His signature outfit is a long crimson royal robe with heart motifs over a white shirt, gold-trimmed, worn with a crown and, at trial, a great white judge's wig with the crown set over it. Signature props: a note-book and round spectacles. Flat, oblong playing-card proportions with arms and legs as a card-king.

quotes.quote: and, last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS.
the judge, by the way, was the King; and as he wore his crown over the wig
the King put on his spectacles and looked anxiously round
The King laid his hand upon her arm, and timidly said “Consider, my dear: she is only a child!”

payload.name: The Knave of Hearts
payload.note: The one playing card called the Knave of Hearts, who carries the King's crown in the procession, is tried for stealing the tarts, and appears as a cardboard figure in Alice's evidence dream; all three entries are the same individual across divisions.

stages.label: The Knave of Hearts
stages.text: The Knave of Hearts: a flat, oblong playing card of cardboard with a head, arms and legs at the corners, young adult, slim build, pale cardboard skin, hair and face painted in simple red-and-white card style, a small heart-marked tunic in red and white with a plain card collar, a crimson velvet cushion carried as his signature prop, simple iron chains at the wrists when on trial.

quotes.quote: oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners
Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King’s crown on a crimson velvet cushion
the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him
being made entirely of cardboard

payload.name: The Queen's playing-card soldiers
payload.note: The ten oblong card soldiers with clubs who march in the procession, form the croquet arches, carry out the Queen's orders, and appear as the court officers who suppress the guinea-pigs and remove the Dormouse; the same card-soldier retinue in each portrayal.

stages.label: Playing-card soldiers
stages.text: The Queen's playing-card soldiers: flat oblong playing cards with a club pattern on the front, each with a small head, arms and legs at the corners, standing in a row of ten. Each card carries a club, with a neat cardboard edge. Their faces are simple painted expressions of stiff, dutiful seriousness. The uniform is a period red and black card-suit livery, with a small crown-style cap on the head. Narrow, straight-edged bodies, with hands and feet tucked at the corners.

quotes.quote: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners

payload.name: the courtiers
payload.note: Ten diamond-decorated card courtiers who walk two by two in the procession.

stages.label: the courtiers
stages.text: the courtiers: a group of ten flat, oblong playing-card courtiers, each a card-shaped body with a head, arms and legs at the corners, ornamented all over with red and white diamonds. Each card has a small, sober, human-like face with a simple painted expression and a plain card-stiff bearing, walking upright in pairs. Their dress is a suggested period courtly tunic and hat, drawn flat in the card's own pattern, with diamond motifs on the body and clothing in the same red and white.

quotes.quote: the ten courtiers; these were ornamented all over with diamonds, and walked two and two
oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners

payload.name: the royal children
payload.note: Ten heart-decorated children who skip hand in hand in the procession.

stages.label: the royal children
stages.text: the royal children: ten young children, drawn as flat oblong playing cards with heads, arms and legs at the corners, their bodies ornamented all over with red hearts; a small group of ten, each child with a simple rounded head and childlike proportions, and the same card pattern on front and back.

quotes.quote: the royal children; there were ten of them, and the little dears came jumping merrily along hand in hand, in couples
they were all ornamented with hearts.

payload.name: the executioner
payload.note: The Queen's executioner who argues about beheading the Cat and runs to fetch the Duchess in unit 70.

stages.label: the executioner
stages.text: the executioner: a flat, oblong playing-card figure with a head, arms and legs, middle-aged and stoutly built, with a close-cropped grey beard and heavy brows, a dark sober face. He wears a black Victorian-era tunic over a waistcoat, with a dark cap and a short axe-shaped tool slung at the hip, in black and grey tones.

quotes.quote: you couldn’t cut off a head unless there was a body to cut it off from
the executioner went off like an arrow

payload.name: the flamingo
payload.note: A live flamingo used as Alice's mallet; it twists its neck and at one point flies off into a tree.

stages.label: the flamingo
stages.text: the flamingo: a live flamingo with long slender pink legs and a long S-curved neck, a sleek body with pale pink feathers and darker pink flight feathers, a long bill tipped with black, and bright, wide-set eyes. It is a bird of the Wonderland croquet-ground, living and wriggling, used as a mallet.

quotes.quote: it _would_ twist itself round and look up in her face
its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down

payload.name: the hedgehogs
payload.note: Live hedgehogs used as croquet balls, which roll away and fight one another.

stages.label: the hedgehogs
stages.text: the hedgehogs: small live hedgehogs with brown-grey spiny backs and short snouts, tiny dark eyes and little legs, shaped into rounded balls when curled up, drawn as animals with no clothing or human features; their spines are the defining feature and they show no face-to-face human expression.

quotes.quote: the balls were live hedgehogs
the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away

payload.name: the Queen's croquet-ground
payload.note: The single walled-garden croquet ground of the Queen, with flamingo mallets and hedgehog balls, where the game and executions take place; both entries describe this same place.

stages.label: The Queen's croquet-ground
stages.text: The Queen's croquet-ground: an enclosed walled garden of uneven ground, ridged and furrowed like ploughed earth, with a few sparse trees and low hedges around its edges. Scattered across the lawn are hedgehog balls and flamingo mallets, with soldier-card arches standing where the hoops would be. Tall flowering shrubs and a pale Victorian sky frame the grounds, with a distant palace-like building behind the garden wall. No people in the scene.

quotes.quote: it was all ridges and furrows; the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes
the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches

payload.name: the Gryphon
payload.note: A single mythical Gryphon who guides Alice to the Mock Turtle, interrupts his story, and appears again in the court; the descriptions differ in wording but depict the same creature.

stages.label: Gryphon
stages.text: the Gryphon: a mythical creature with the head and forelegs of an eagle and the hindquarters of a lion, feathered wings folded at its back, a curved yellow beak and sharp talons, its body covered in tawny fur and golden-brown feathers; it sits upright on its haunches in sunlight with its front paws raised as if gesturing, its manner languid and pert, its colouring warm gold and russet.

quotes.quote: They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun.
the Gryphon went on in a deep voice

payload.name: the Mock Turtle
payload.note: A sorrowful, sobbing creature with a calf's head and a turtle's tail or flappers, who tells of his schooldays in the sea, the Lobster Quadrille and the whiting, and sings 'Beautiful Soup'; the two entries are the same character across divisions, distinguished from other names in the group only by being this single individual.

stages.label: The Mock Turtle
stages.text: The Mock Turtle: a sorrowful creature with a calf's head and a turtle's tail, with flappers for forelimbs. Middle-aged, heavy-set build, sad large eyes, grey-white calf's head with a soft muzzle. Wears a dull waistcoat and a dark coat, with a turtle's shell-patterned tail. Carries nothing.

quotes.quote: sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock
Once," said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, "I was a real Turtle.
with tears running down his cheeks

payload.name: the old Turtle master (Tortoise)
payload.note: The old Turtle who taught the Mock Turtle at school under the sea; only recalled in the Mock Turtle's story, not present on stage.

payload.name: the Drawling-master (old conger-eel)
payload.note: The old conger-eel who came once a week to teach Drawling, Stretching and Fainting in Coils; recalled in the Mock Turtle's story only.

payload.name: the Classics master (old crab)
payload.note: The old crab who taught the Gryphon the Classics, recalled only in the Mock Turtle's story and never present; kept apart from the Caucus-race Crab because the notes give no sign they are the same individual.

payload.name: the rock ledge by the sea
payload.note: The lonely rock ledge where the Mock Turtle sits sobbing and tells his story, near the sea.

stages.label: the rock ledge by the sea
stages.text: the rock ledge by the sea: a small, weathered ledge of grey rock jutting out over the water at the edge of a sea shore, its rough surface bare and lonely, with waves breaking on rocks below and open sea stretching beyond, no trees or buildings in sight.

quotes.quote: sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock
living at the bottom of the sea

payload.name: the undersea school
payload.note: The school under the sea attended by the Mock Turtle in his youth, existing only in his recollection; not shown on stage.

stages.label: The undersea school
stages.text: The undersea school: a schoolhouse on the sea floor, seen only in the Mock Turtle's memory; pale sandy bottom, drifting sea-green water above, dim filtered light, faint coral and kelp at its edges, no people or animals present.

quotes.quote: we went to school in the sea
living at the bottom of the sea

payload.name: Whiting
payload.note: A sea fish addressed in the Mock Turtle's song; it urges a snail to join the dance. Described as the subject of the song, not a physical presence on stage.

payload.name: Snail
payload.note: A snail in the Mock Turtle's song who refuses the whiting's invitation to join the dance, saying 'Too far, too far!'.

payload.name: Porpoise
payload.note: A porpoise in the song who treads on the whiting's tail; mentioned in the whiting's explanation and in the Mock Turtle's remark about fish needing a porpoise.

payload.name: Lobsters
payload.note: Sea creatures who serve as partners in the Lobster Quadrille; they are thrown out to sea and sing of their dance in the song.

payload.name: Sea-shore
payload.note: The undersea setting where the Lobster Quadrille would be danced along the shore and where the whiting and lobsters are placed.

stages.label: Sea-shore
stages.text: Sea-shore: an undersea shore of pale shingle and wet sand sloping down to a dim, rolling sea, with rock outcrops and clumps of swaying sea-weed and kelp along the tide-line. Scattered jelly-fish drift in the shallows, and a faint far shore lies across the water in the murky distance. No people.

quotes.quote: you first form into a line along the sea-shore
They are waiting on the shingle
when you've cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way

payload.name: Court of Justice
aliases: the court of the Queen of Hearts
payload.note: The open court of the Queen of Hearts, with throne, jury-box and table of tarts, where the trial is held; the Lobster Quadrille entry is the same court heard in the distance before it is shown on stage.

stages.label: Court of Justice
stages.text: Court of Justice: an open court of hall-like space with a raised throne at one end, a tall jury-box beside it, and a long central table in the middle holding a large dish of tarts. Wooden benches and a crowded floor of stone surround the table, with a rail and doorways at the edges. Wall hangings and dim banners frame the room, and a high ceiling holds the dream-court's brightness.

quotes.quote: In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it
she tipped over the jury-box with the edge of her skirt

payload.name: the jury
payload.note: The twelve jurors (birds and beasts writing on slates) who act together as one body in the court; both divisions describe the same jury, so the entries are joined.

stages.label: the jury
stages.text: the jury: twelve small creatures, a mix of birds and beasts, seated in the jury-box, each animal standing or sitting upright with human posture and dress in Victorian period waistcoats and small hats, a slate and pencil held before each one. Ages mixed and mostly small and adult; builds slight and compact; plumage or fur in muted tones of brown, grey and cream; the Lizard among them has green-grey scaly skin and a long tail. Signature props: a slate and slate-pencil each.

quotes.quote: those twelve creatures
some of them were animals, and some were birds
The twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates.
it was Bill, the Lizard

payload.name: The pack of cards (the court's playing cards)
payload.note: The playing cards of the Queen's court who rise up and fly down at Alice, ending the dream; told apart from the jury by being playing cards in the dream rather than jurors in the trial.

stages.label: The pack of cards
stages.text: The pack of cards: a crowd of flat, oblong playing cards, each with a small head, arms and legs, in the Queen's court suits of hearts and spades with painted court-card dress and simple cardboard edges, each card a thin, stiff sheet with no depth.

quotes.quote: You’re nothing but a pack of cards!
At this the whole pack rose up into the air, and came flying down upon her
